title: Weekly play
hook: play is practice too; David dances before the ark with all his might and tells Michal he will play before the LORD
tomorrow: a monk spread 150 psalms across a week. why not one day?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: screen-free. The seventh-day field held no manna, and the rest was a gift. Today, another gift that rarely makes it onto the calendar.

When did you last do something only because it was fun? Not useful fun. Just fun. King David once did it in front of a whole city. The ark of God is coming up into Jerusalem with shouting and the sound of the trumpet, and David dances before it with all his might, girded with a linen ephod, leaping. His wife Michal watches from a window, and the text says she despised him in her heart.
screen: `ONLY BECAUSE IT WAS FUN.` → `THE ARK COMES TO JERUSALEM.` → `DAVID DANCES WITH ALL HIS MIGHT.` → `MICHAL WATCHES FROM THE WINDOW.`

segments.voice: She meets him at the door. How glorious was the king today, she says, uncovering himself like a fool in front of the servant girls. And David answers: it was before the LORD, "therefore will I play before the LORD." He doesn't apologize. He says he'll be even less dignified than that. David's answer carries a teaching: in the Hebrew Bible, joy before God is worship, and it uses the body, not only the mind. The last psalm calls for it: "Praise him with the timbrel and dance." Jewish life keeps that alive. On Simchat Torah, the day the cycle of Torah readings ends and starts again from the beginning, people carry the scrolls around the synagogue and dance with them, circle after circle, children on shoulders, nobody grading the steps. Joy isn't the opposite of holiness there. It's one of its shapes. So weekly play isn't a break from practice. In David's story it can be practice. The part of you that worries how it looks gets set down for a while, the way David set down the king. Play is the self that forgets it's being watched. That's why it belongs on the calendar, beside the silence and the study, and why it's fine to be bad at it.
screen: `THEREFORE WILL I PLAY BEFORE THE LORD.` · `JOY BEFORE GOD IS WORSHIP.` · `PRAISE HIM WITH THE TIMBREL AND DANCE.` · `SIMCHAT TORAH: DANCING WITH THE SCROLLS.` · then, large: `PLAY.`

segments.voice: Stand up and move for a minute in a way that feels a little silly: sway, tap a rhythm on your legs, step side to side to a song in your head. Let it be unimpressive. Then sit, feel your heartbeat, and choose one hour of play for this week.
Weekly play: an hour each week of doing something for joy, the way David played before the LORD, without checking who's at the window.
Here's the line: play. David danced with all his might, and he didn't apologize to anyone. That's today.

screen: `DAY 1628 COUNTS.` → `THE WEEKLY PRACTICE · 9 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: A MONK SPREAD 150 PSALMS ACROSS A WEEK. WHY NOT ONE DAY?`

howItsDone: On Simchat Torah, Jewish congregations carry the Torah scrolls around the synagogue in circles of singing and dancing; people who keep a weekly play hour often choose a game, a dance class, music or a sport done for its own sake.
